balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For China Resources Pharmaceutical Group Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For China Resources Pharmaceutical Group Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For China Resources Pharmaceutical Group Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For China Resources Pharmaceutical Group Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For China Resources Pharmaceutical Group Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For China Resources Pharmaceutical Group Limited: the blended margin here is mostly a segment-mix effect, not a single business getting more or less efficient -- distribution's ~6% margin dilutes manufacturing's ~60% gross margin because distribution is ~79% of revenue. A rising blended margin usually means manufacturing (or retail) is growing its revenue share faster than distribution; see the segment-mix charts below for the split.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin
  • Whether margin moves track the segment revenue mix shift

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For China Resources Pharmaceutical Group Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For China Resources Pharmaceutical Group Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For China Resources Pharmaceutical Group Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below. Consolidated revenue is dominated by the low-margin distribution segment (~79% of FY2025 revenue) -- see the segment-mix charts below for the part of the business that actually drives profit.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

segmentRevenue.title: Revenue by segment
segmentRevenue.content:
China Resources Pharmaceutical Group reports three segments: manufacturing (branded and generic drugs it produces), distribution (wholesale of its own and third-party pharmaceuticals to hospitals and pharmacies) and retail (its own pharmacy chain).

For CR Pharmaceutical: distribution is the overwhelming majority of revenue (~79% in FY2025) simply by the nature of wholesale pass-through volumes, but it is a thin-margin logistics business. Manufacturing is only ~17% of revenue. Retail is the smallest segment (~4.5%) but the fastest-growing, as the pharmacy footprint expands.

What to watch:

  • Manufacturing revenue growth -- it is the segment where pricing power and product mix (not just volume) can move the needle
  • Retail's growth rate relative to the other two, as a proxy for store network expansion
  • Distribution revenue growing without a matching gain in segment result (see below) -- pure volume growth at a flat thin margin adds little value

segmentResult.title: Segment result (profit) by segment
segmentResult.content:
Segment result is each segment's operating profit before unallocated corporate costs and tax -- the profit measure management itself uses to judge the three businesses.

For CR Pharmaceutical: this is the heart of the investment case. Manufacturing runs at roughly 60% gross margin and generates about two-thirds of total segment result from under a fifth of revenue. Distribution, despite being ~79% of revenue, contributes only around a third of segment result at a thin ~6% margin -- it is closer to a logistics business than a pharma business. Retail is the smallest profit contributor today but is scaling fastest.

What to watch:

  • Manufacturing's share of segment result rising or falling -- a rising share means the higher-quality earnings stream is growing faster than the low-margin distribution bulk
  • Distribution result staying flat or declining even as its revenue grows (margin compression from procurement reform / hospital pricing pressure)
  • Retail result turning consistently positive and scaling with store/revenue growth

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For China Resources Pharmaceutical Group Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
